t: You're at Park Crescent, a sweeping semicircle of stuccoed terraced houses at the north end of Portland Place, just south of Marylebone Road. It was designed by John Nash as part of his Roman-inspired approach to Regent's Park. It was first imagined as a full circle, to be called Regent's Circus, but Park Square was built to the north instead. Only garden buildings face the park, so the upper floors enjoy a long green view. Clementina Drummond, first wife of the Earl of Airlie, died here in 1835.
